subject.title: fix(cron): keep isolated run status ok when delivery fails

question: Should successful isolated cron execution with post-run delivery failure be recorded as `status=ok` plus `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`, or should OpenClaw preserve error semantics or introduce a warning status first?
rationale: The code change is narrow and tested, but the choice changes scheduler backoff, failure alerts, and external operator semantics for undelivered successful runs.

options.title: Land focused decoupling
options.body: Accept `status=ok` for successful execution and require delivery-aware consumers to use `deliveryStatus` and `lastDeliveryError` for undelivered runs.

options.title: Prefer warning status
options.body: Pause this PR and pursue the broader `warning` status model after resolving protocol, UI, CLI, and plugin compatibility.

options.title: Keep error semantics
options.body: Reject the decoupling for now so delivery failures continue to trigger existing error/backoff/failure-alert paths.

recommendation.title: Land focused decoupling
recommendation.body: Accept `status=ok` for successful execution and require delivery-aware consumers to use `deliveryStatus` and `lastDeliveryError` for undelivered runs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the cron status/delivery boundary, and this is a status-contract decision rather than a mechanical code repair.
